doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

chapter: The new jazz and its audience
title: Ascension liner notes and submitting to art
summary: His Ascension liner note and the need to submit to art.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: This morning I was reading that comment that I just read to you about breaking down tonal centers and I got this little flash I said, I remember reading something about a liner note that said something about be advised that this record cannot be loved or understood in one sitting. So I went and got my “Ascension” LP and there you were. And you said that this is a “guaranteed soul rinsing.” So I find it interesting what you just said about John Coltrane and trying to make people saints.

Yeah you have to submit to art sometimes, you know what I mean? You have to give up all your expectation and basically even your sense of self and submit to the work itself in order to receive it fully. It’s an experience on both ends that is not entirely rational but largely intuitional. And so it takes a certain kind of discipline to be able to do that. But people who don’t listen to music all the time seriously, then it can be hard to have that experience and to have the music work for you in a way that the musicians intended. But if you can do that, if you can give yourself up to it and just sort of fly with them, they’ll take you somewhere.
